_comment: xLSTM retune campaign. The gru/lstm/transformer arch screen is already done (v0.38-v0.47); this sweep is the xLSTM follow-up. Run with: uv run python scripts/train_campaign.py --sweep sweep_arch.json [--dry-run]. Each run auto-versions into checkpoints/v<version>/ and is gauntleted (tournament block) against baselines + resnet/temporal incumbents, so it slots into the same Elo ladder. defaults set history=1 (temporal archs ignore stacked history) and pin the temporal + xlstm knobs; each run overrides network.arch=xlstm plus the knobs it varies. Design assumptions from the 80k Elo of the other archs: (a) lr=1e-4 beat the ResNet-tuned 5e-5 by ~+97 Elo for BOTH gru (592->688) and transformer (737->834, best temporal net), so we transfer it and use it as the base for the exploration axes; (b) eta=0.2 was mixed (helped gru, hurt transformer) -> one symmetry probe; (c) extra mixer depth was arch-dependent (helped gru +98, hurt transformer -228) -> one risky native-depth probe. The xLSTM-specific axis is the mLSTM/sLSTM composition (network.xlstm_slstm_at): since transformer (~ mLSTM parallel matrix-memory) beat gru (~ sLSTM gated recurrence), we sweep all-mLSTM (fastest on the vanilla sLSTM backend) vs mixed vs all-sLSTM. Screening at 80k to match the canonical horizon.

runs._comment: Control: canonical ResNet-tuned lr=5e-5, default 2-block [mLSTM, sLSTM] stack. Reference point for the lr transfer.
runs.name: arch-xlstm-base

runs._comment: lr transfer: the +97-Elo win seen on gru AND transformer. Highest-confidence single bet; also the base lr for the exploration variants below.
runs.name: arch-xlstm-lr1e4

runs._comment: All-mLSTM (slstm_at=[] -> 2 mLSTM blocks): the most transformer-like, fully parallel matrix-memory variant, and the fastest on the vanilla sLSTM backend. Tests whether mLSTM's transformer-like memory drives xLSTM here.
runs.name: arch-xlstm-mlstm

runs._comment: All-sLSTM (slstm_at=[0,1] -> 2 sLSTM blocks): the recurrent, gated-memory extreme. Opposite pole from -mlstm; brackets the composition axis at the transferred lr.
runs.name: arch-xlstm-slstm

runs._comment: Deeper native stack: 4 blocks, paper-style alternation [mLSTM, sLSTM, mLSTM, sLSTM]. Depth was arch-dependent for the other nets (helped gru, hurt transformer); xLSTM is a native deep-block arch, so one probe.
runs.name: arch-xlstm-4L

runs._comment: Regularization symmetry probe: eta=0.2 vs the canonical 0.5, holding the transferred lr. eta was mixed on the other archs.
runs.name: arch-xlstm-eta0.2
